migrate.title: Migrate this repository?
migrate.body: This starts a migration Run to {target}. The repository is ready: it has no blockers and no open tasks that must be done first.

run_anyway.title: Run this repository anyway?
run_anyway.body: This starts a migration Run to {target} without waiting for the open tasks to be done. The Run can leave work for you to finish by hand.
run_anyway.warning: {count, plural, =0 {No tasks are open.} one {# open task will not be done by the Run.} other {# open tasks will not be done by the Run.}}

resync.title: Resync this repository?
resync.body: This runs the migration again to bring {target} up to date with the source.

verify.title: Verify this repository?
verify.body: This compares the source and {target} again and updates the parity result. It changes nothing on either side.

source_read_only.title: Make the source read-only?
source_read_only.body: This stops further pushes to the source repository. You can undo it later. {target} is not changed.

force_adopt.title: Force adopt the target?
force_adopt.body: The target {target} already exists and has content that this migration did not create. A forced adoption makes it match the source: every source branch and tag is force-pushed, and branches and tags that are not on the source are deleted.
force_adopt.warning: Content on the target that is not on the source is lost. This cannot be undone by a rollback.

rollback.title: Roll back this migration?
rollback.bodyCreated: This deletes the target repository {target}, which this migration created, and everything in it. Deleting it needs the right to delete repositories on the target.
rollback.bodyAdopted: This undoes what the migration changed on the target in reverse order: it deletes the settings, hooks, keys, grants and variables it created and closes its change requests. The repository and its git history stay as they are.
rollback.warning: A rollback cannot be undone. The repository returns to the rolled back status.
rollback.undoFirstBody: The source was made read-only. It must be writable again before the migration can be rolled back. This starts a Run that undoes it; when it has finished, choose Roll back again.

legacy.title: Confirm where this migration's earlier changes are
legacy.body: This migration changed the target before the framework recorded where its changes were made, and the Route's target may have changed since. Continue only if the Route still points at that place: type {name} to confirm it.
legacy.warning: If the earlier changes are elsewhere, cancel. Restore the Route's target to that place, roll the migration back, then change the Route.

undo_source_read_only.title: Undo source read-only?
undo_source_read_only.body: This makes the source repository writable again, so pushes to it are possible once more.

mark_complete.title: Mark this repository complete?
mark_complete.body: Use this when the repository was finished by hand. The status becomes manually completed; you can revoke it later.

revoke_complete.title: Revoke the manual completion?
revoke_complete.body: The computed status returns: verified if parity is equal and no task is open, otherwise the outcome of the last Run.
